title: BECE Business Studies: Book-keeping - Business Studies - Cash Book
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The principal book of account used primarily to record all daily receipts and payments of cash and cheques is called the:
questions.explain: A **cash book** is the financial journal that contains all cash receipts and payments, including bank deposits and withdrawals. It is a book of prime entry used exclusively for cash and bank transactions.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The Cash Book is uniquely classified in accounting because it serves as both a book of prime entry and a:
questions.explain: The Cash Book is unique because it fulfills a dual role: it is a **book of original entry** (where transactions are recorded first) and it also serves directly as the cash and bank **ledger accounts** in the general ledger system.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A Single Column Cash Book is designed to record:
options: only cash receipts and cash payments
questions.explain: A **Single Column Cash Book** has only one amount column on each side (debit and credit) and is strictly used to record **only physical cash receipts and cash payments**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following statements is a fundamental rule regarding the cash column of a cash book?
options: It can show a credit balance at the end of the month.
It must always show a debit balance or a nil balance.
It records only transactions involving commercial banks.
It is used to write off bad debts from credit customers.
questions.explain: A business cannot spend more physical cash than it has. Therefore, the **cash column must always show a debit balance** (meaning receipts are greater than payments) or a zero balance, but never a credit balance.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A Two-Column Cash Book differs from a Single Column Cash Book because it contains extra columns for:
questions.explain: A **Two-Column Cash Book** contains two amount columns on each side: one for **cash** transactions and one for **bank** transactions (cheques).
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In a cash book, what does a transaction recorded on both the debit side (cash column) and credit side (bank column) represent?
questions.explain: A **contra entry** occurs when a transaction involves both the cash and bank accounts. For example, withdrawing cash from the bank for office use is credited to the bank column and debited to the cash column in the same cash book.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following letters is traditionally placed in the folio column of a cash book to denote a contra entry?
questions.explain: The letter **'C'** is written in the folio column against a contra entry to indicate that the double-entry for that specific transaction has been completed within the cash book itself and needs no posting to a ledger.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following transactions would result in a contra entry in a Two-Column Cash Book?
options: Depositing office cash into the bank account
Buying office stationery with physical cash
questions.explain: **Depositing office cash into the bank** increases the bank balance (debit bank) and decreases the office cash (credit cash). Since both accounts are in the Two-Column Cash Book, it forms a **contra entry**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In order to prepare a Three-Column Cash Book, which column must be added to the standard cash and bank columns?
questions.explain: A **Three-Column Cash Book** features three amount columns on both sides: Cash, Bank, and **Discount** (Discount Allowed on the debit side and Discount Received on the credit side).
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In a Three-Column Cash Book, the discount column on the debit (receipts) side is specifically used to record:
options: discount allowed to debtors for prompt payment
questions.explain: The debit side records receipts. When receiving payment from customers (debtors), the business may give them a discount for paying early. This is called **Discount Allowed** and is recorded in the debit-side discount column.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A trader starts the week with a cash balance of $₦45,000$. During the week, she makes cash sales of $₦12,000$, pays wages of $₦8,000$ in cash, and banks $₦15,000$ cash. What is the closing cash balance?
questions.explain:
To calculate the closing cash balance, sum the receipts and subtract the payments:

1.  **Opening Balance**: $₦45,000$
2.  **Add Receipts**: $+ ₦12,000$ (Cash sales)
    *   Total cash available = $₦57,000$
3.  **Less Payments**: $₦8,000$ (Wages) $+ ₦15,000$ (Cash banked)
    *   Total payments = $₦23,000$
4.  **Closing Balance**: $₦57,000 - ₦23,000 = ₦34,000$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The bank column of a cash book shows total debit entries (receipts) of $₦150,000$ and total credit entries (payments) of $₦180,000$. This indicates a:
questions.explain: If payments ($₦180,000$) exceed receipts ($₦150,000$) in the bank column, it means the business has drawn out more money than it has in the account. This negative balance of **₦30,000** is known as a **bank overdraft**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A customer who owes the business $₦20,000$ settles his account by paying a cheque of $₦19,000$ in full settlement. How will this be entered on the debit side of a Three-Column Cash Book?
options: ₦20,000 in the bank column and ₦1,000 in the discount column
₦19,000 in the bank column and ₦1,000 in the discount column
₦19,000 in the cash column and ₦19,000 in the bank column
₦20,000 in the discount column and ₦19,000 in the cash column
questions.explain: Since a cheque was received, $₦19,000$ goes into the **bank column**. The difference between the debt ($₦20,000$) and the payment ($₦19,000$) is a cash discount allowed to the customer, so $₦1,000$ goes into the **discount column**.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A business buys goods worth $₦40,000$ and receives a $5\%$ cash discount for immediate payment by cheque. What amount will be entered in the bank column on the credit side?
questions.explain:
First, calculate the discount: 
$$5\% \times ₦40,000 = ₦2,000$$
Next, subtract the discount from the total amount to find the cheque payment:
$$₦40,000 - ₦2,000 = ₦38,000$$
The actual payment of **₦38,000** is recorded in the bank column.
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q:
Study the extract from the debit side of a Cash Book below:

| Date | Particulars | Discount (₦) | Cash (₦) | Bank (₦) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| May 10 | B. Chidi | 500 | | 8,500 |

What is the total value of the debt settled by B. Chidi on May 10?
questions.explain:
To find the total original debt, you must add the cheque payment received to the cash discount that was allowed.
$$\text{Total Debt} = \text{Amount Paid} + \text{Discount Allowed}$$
$$\text{Total Debt} = ₦8,500 + ₦500 = ₦9,000$$
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Unlike the cash and bank columns, the discount columns in a Three-Column Cash Book are not balanced at the end of the period. Instead, they are:
options: subtracted from each other to find profit
transferred to the petty cash book
totalled and posted directly to the discount accounts in the ledger
cancelled out to prevent a contra entry
questions.explain: The discount columns do not represent an asset like cash or bank, so they are not "balanced c/d". They are purely memorandum columns that are **totalled** at the end of the month, and those totals are posted to the *Discount Allowed* and *Discount Received* accounts in the General Ledger.
questions.subject: Business Studies
